bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/route_discovery.rs (discovery point and ReceiverFeed); no extension host or system route picker integration
summary: Apple's framework lets an app extension feed third-party media receivers into the system AirPlay-style device picker, running inside Apple's system sandbox. BifrOSt has a model for the extension point, receiver metadata, events, TTL and authorization, but it does not run a discovery extension process, open network browse sockets or present a system device picker.

features.note: The SDK declares a namespaced point and explicit start/stop feed state. It does not load an app extension into a system sandbox or bind lifecycle to picker visibility.
Headless events report newly found and expired receivers. A refresh is silent; there is no event delivery into a system picker.

features.apple: DDDevice, DDDevice.Category, DDDeviceState, DDDevice.Protocol, media playback state
features.note: Receiver ID, display name, host, port and last-seen time are modelled and validated. Apple category, protocol and playback-state metadata are not represented.
The model reports invalid owner, zero TTL and malformed receiver fields; it has no extension-host or transport error domain.
The app sandbox exists, but it has no entitlement that lets an app add a receiver to a system picker.

gaps: No system device picker or route picker view that lists third-party media receivers; the SDK feed is not wired to a shell browse service.
No sandboxed extension process or transport that feeds the modeled discovery point.
AirPlay & Handoff exists only as a settings page (springboard/src/shell/pages.rs:598) with no receiver discovery behind it.
